_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; credkit.Start is the first statement of each main and credkit.Exit the last; the API client goes through credkit.Transport under the origin pin; feedback, deliver and the doctor probe are built on it; every file write except the 0600 credential store and config.toml goes through the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile is that declared exemption, listed in Declarations.Files); children run through credkit.RunCommand. Retired, reason replaced by the shared credential kit: secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. Origins: only the base URL the run really uses. A credential goes nowhere else, the MCP HTTP bearers go nowhere at all, and Files lists only the run's own config, because the first base_url listed becomes the allowed origin: a discovered default under an explicit selection, another --home and a store recording an issued base URL are held, not listed. Tests: internal/exoblackbox (built binaries over TLS against a stub that echoes every credential), TestFilesListOnlyWhatTheRunReads, TestReadPathsCoversEveryFileLoadReads.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the credkit wiring from a per-connector declarations file, so a reprint keeps it by construction.

handfixes.summary: Every SQLite handle goes through credkit.SQLDriver: internal/credsql registers the one driver and every sql.Open in store.go and platform/migration.go names it, the MCP sql tool's read-only opener included. The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to a DSN parameter credsql applies as each connection opens.
handfixes.why: A statement's text and bound values are a sink of their own, reads included. Closes credential-split-across-sql-bindings: a held value split across two bound values of one statement is one unit to the driver. Replaces the connector-only WithholdingSQLiteDriver.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing, then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it: a token holding the word unauthorized made a GET /mcp without Authorization return a piece of the held token.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the inner, kit-wrapped handler and only a write-free preflight runs before credkit.MCPHTTP.

handfixes.summary: No handle from a raw open writes a byte past the credential kit. The lock file stays empty; the journal's lines and repair newline go through credkit.AppendFile; the fingerprint key through credkit.WriteFile. TestEveryFileWriteGoesThroughTheKit walks every function's handles with go/ast, so a raw Write, io.Copy, Fprint or a handle stored behind an interface fails it.
handfixes.why: A scan of raw opens alone allows a handle that then writes. A response holding a one-character credential would otherwise put that byte in a lock file, past the kit. A reprint re-emits these writers; these asserts and the scan catch it.

handfixes.summary: Every credential a response carries is held before any command reads the body, then replaced by name so a listing stays readable. The name rule is one shared walker over response bodies, request bodies, MCP arguments and --stdin bodies, any depth, every spelling. A mask is judged by shape only. No Exchange cmdlet property in the spec matches a credential name, so mailbox names, GUIDs, UPNs and Identity are never held.
handfixes.why: The kit withholds a whole unit that repeats a held value, so a body carrying a credential member would print nothing if the member were not replaced first; the kit holds declared names only, the walker also holds duplicate members and every document in a body. responseHoldTripper reads each response under the client size cap and decodes it as the client will (client/exo_decode.go is kept for this: the kit does not do name-rule replacement). Tests: TestResponseCredentialsHeldAndReplacedByName, TestRedactBodyAndHoldByName, TestRealisticListingsSurviveUnwithheld.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal writes through the kit, EXCHANGE_ONLINE_LEARN_SESSION is hashed under its own prefix, argv_shape and failed_flag record only flag names the invoked command declares (any other is a placeholder), and teach_playbook's error log counts arguments rather than repeating them.
handfixes.why: A mistyped flag can be a pasted token, and a session label can be anything the harness set: both reached the journal file as written.

handfixes.summary: A run profile holds no credential: a credential-named flag value is dropped when profiles.json loads, and credwire holds the file's values before output.
handfixes.why: Kit item 8c. profiles.json is written by the program but can be edited by hand, and its values become flags on later runs. Tests: TestRunProfileKeepsNoCredential.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a read-only cmdlet (Get-AcceptedDomain, POST /adminapi/beta/<tenant>/InvokeCommand) with the real credential. 401 is rejected, 403 limited, 404 a base URL that is not the Exchange API (naming EXCHANGE_ONLINE_BASE_URL), instead of calling any HTTP response reachable and never checking the credential. Every verdict word prints in clear.
handfixes.why: doctor is the command every doc tells an operator to run, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. A cmdlet API has no GET to probe, so the generic walk does not apply; a token's own tid names the tenant, and an opaque token probes the zero GUID.

handfixes.summary: A token named on this run (EXCHANGE_ONLINE_TOKEN) wins over a stored auth_header, on a write, on both binaries.
handfixes.why: The generated AuthHeader prefers a stored header, so an operator rotating a key by environment kept sending the old one. Under the kit that is also a refused send. Test: TestNamedTokenWinsOverAStoredOne.

handfixes.summary: Before anything prints, credwire holds a key pasted on the auth set-token line, the piped set-token value, and the credential fields of a --stdin body, and gives the program the same bytes on a new os.Stdin. It does not use the kit's StdinFlags: those hold every line of a body, so a pretty-printed body stops the program and a one-line body withholds its own preview.
handfixes.why: Kit item 8a. A parser error repeats what it was given before the command reads the pipe. Test: TestStdinHeldBeforeTheFirstByte.

handfixes.summary: Exchange admin endpoints are cmdlet RPC over POST: the spec writes each cmdlet as <surface path>#<Cmdlet>, and a client hook turns the fragment plus the command's body into {"CmdletInput":{"CmdletName":...,"Parameters":...}}, routes with X-AnchorMailbox, sends Accept-Encoding identity, follows @odata.nextLink pages on the same origin only, and returns the merged value rows. A query the shared client appended after the fragment (the read tool's properties, carried as $select) is moved to the real query string.
handfixes.why: The spec cannot express a cmdlet envelope (net/http never sends a URL fragment); without the hook every command POSTs the bare parameters to the wrong body shape. Sources: learn.microsoft.com/exchange/reference/admin-api-get-started and CIPP-API New-ExoRequest.ps1. Hand file internal/cli/exo_transport.go, installed by exo_guard.go's registerClientHook UNDER the origin pin (the envelope transport wraps the pinned one, so every page it sends is pinned). Tests: internal/cli/exo_transport_test.go, TestOriginPinCoversEveryCmdletPage.

handfixes.summary: 30 generated endpoint commands carry a runnable Example (tenant GUID plus the cmdlet's identity flags); which.go WhyItMatters lines no longer stop at "v2."; helpers.go drops the dead retainCLIQueryParams pair.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.x emits an Example only when every input has one; cmdlet parameters are body flags with no spec example, so dogfood's example coverage and the agent-facing help need these. Carried from the 4.33.5 print (polish). Re-applied by tools/apply_handfixes.sh (handfix-4342/generated-hand-edits.patch); a reprint that drops them shows in dogfood example coverage and in these asserts.

asserts.contains: WhyItMatters: "Organization MailTips settings and limits (Admin API v2.0)."

handfixes.summary: The press spec (withheld from this repo) carries x-pp-mutation on every operation: false on the 39 Get-* cmdlets, true on the 21 others (Set, Add, Remove, Enable, Disable, Release, Delete, Clear). Every endpoint is a POST, so the cmdlet verb, not the method, classifies reads: exchange-online_read serves the Get-* cmdlets (also under EXCHANGE_ONLINE_MCP_READ_ONLY=1) and refuses the rest, and exchange-online_execute previews every write until confirm is boolean true.
handfixes.why: Spec-encoded, so it survives a reprint by construction. Work order blocker: MCP read-only mode blocked reads until reads were classified by cmdlet verb; press 4.34.2 honours x-pp-mutation natively (the create alias on read POSTs is gone too). TestEveryStateChangingCmdletNeedsConfirm (internal/mcp/exo_writes_confirm_test.go) checks the generated endpoint table by verb. The spec is not vendored here, so the asserts read the generated endpoint table in internal/mcp/code_orch.go.

handfixes.summary: Every API request, redirect hop and @odata.nextLink page goes only to the scheme, host and port of the configured API base URL (EXCHANGE_ONLINE_BASE_URL, default https://outlook.office365.com); anything else is refused before it is resolved, dialled or given the bearer token.
handfixes.why: Work order host pinning. originPinTripper and the same check FIRST in CheckRedirect (hand file internal/cli/exo_guard.go, registered with registerClientHook, so every CLI, novel fan-out and MCP client gets it), installed under the cmdlet transport so its nextLink pages are pinned too (the transport's own sameOrigin check stays). Byte-exact ASCII-folded origins; a host with a non-ASCII byte never matches. Tests: TestOriginPinRefusesRedirectToAnotherHost, TestOriginPinCoversEveryCmdletPage, TestNormalizedOriginRefusesNonASCIIAndFillsPorts, TestRedirectNeverReachesAnotherHost (black-box, CLI and MCP).

handfixes.summary: The on-disk response cache is off on every client: raw cmdlet bodies never sit in cache files.
handfixes.why: Work order: nothing but the credential store holds a credential. c.NoCache = true in guardClient (exo_guard.go); TestOriginPinCoversEveryCmdletPage asserts it.

handfixes.summary: Every resource write passes mergeIncomingResourceData, which redacts credential-named values at any depth, whether or not anything held them, so a mailbox row stays a row. A record that cannot be decoded is stored as {}. A held value anywhere else in a statement is the kit's SQL driver's to refuse (credkit-sqlite-every-handle).
handfixes.why: Work order: no credential in files. The kit refuses a statement that repeats a held value, but it does not know a credential-named member nothing held: the strip keeps those out of rows. Covered by TestStoreRedactsCredentialMembersByName and TestNoCredentialInAnyWrittenFile (.db files scanned).

handfixes.summary: Mirrored MCP tools that can change Exchange state (offboard, any later non-read-only command) preview and send only with confirm: true; offboard's preview is its own --plan (reads the mailbox, reports each step done or pending, changes nothing). The preview owns its flag: a caller argument naming it (plan, dry-run) is dropped from the preview whatever its value (Codex review r1 class preview-overridable-by-argument: plan "false" followed the injected --plan and the preview sent). A refused argument is an error naming it, with no note telling the caller to send it.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 gates exchange-online_execute on confirm, but the Cobra-tree mirror registered offboard with no confirm: an MCP call converted a mailbox to shared, hid it, removed devices and granted access at once. RequireConfirmForMirroredWrites (hand file internal/mcp/cobratree/exo_confirm.go), called from RegisterTools after RegisterAll, wraps every mirrored tool that is not read-only, mcp:local-write or local-only; the exo:preview-flag annotation names a command's own boolean read-only flag as its preview. Only boolean true sends; confirm is never forwarded. Tests: TestRegisteredMirroredWritesNeedConfirm, TestPreviewFlagRunsThePlan, TestMirroredWriteNeedsBooleanConfirm, TestMCPWritesNeedConfirm (black-box).

handfixes.summary: access-map counts a trustee the cmdlet rendered by any identifier the user carries (address, name, alias, GUID, ExternalDirectoryObjectId, DistinguishedName, Identity), through the one identifier check recipient.answers.
handfixes.why: Codex review r1 (class trustee-object-id-unmatched): Exchange Online renders GrantSendOnBehalfTo as GUIDs unless the display-name switch is used (vendor-docs/psref/get-distributiongroup.md -IncludeGrantSendOnBehalfToWithDisplayNames; Get-Mailbox has the same switch), and the trustee prefilter accepted only addresses and names, so a real SendOnBehalf grant was missing from both access and ambiguous. Hand file internal/cli/access_map.go. Test: TestAccessMapMatchesTrusteeObjectIDs.

handfixes.summary: Exchange Online is Microsoft-hosted with a public certificate, so the generated EXCHANGE_ONLINE_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY read is removed: no environment value can turn off certificate checks for the admin token. The explicit --insecure flag stays.
handfixes.why: The admin token authorizes mailbox and permission changes; a stray environment value must not expose it to an on-path host. Same reasoning as the fortinet and unifi-network carve-outs, with no self-hosted audience to serve.

handfixes.summary: The MCP forwarding_audit tool is a pure read: --sweep is dropped from its schema and rejected as an argument, and inbox_rules_sweep is the one tool that sweeps. The CLI keeps --sweep.
handfixes.why: A sweep writes the local store. With sweep off the tool only sends Get-* cmdlets, and every Exchange call is a POST, so the read-only gate cannot tell them from writes; one read tool in both modes also leaves the CLI and MCP surfaces with one clear rule.

handfixes.summary: Every request this connector sends reaches the credential kit in the one form the kit reads: cliutil.KitReadableRequest rewrites the query to canonical pairs with the same decoded values and fails that one call, aloud and with no retry, for a query that cannot be decoded, a body-coding header, a Content-Type other than JSON, a URL with no host, or a server-written user name or password. The origin pin runs it on every API request, redirect hops included; deliver and feedback run it on the URL they are given. The cmdlet transport normalizes the first request and each @odata.nextLink through cliutil.CanonicalQuery, and the repeat guard compares the normalized link.
handfixes.why: The kit answers any other request by marking every value unknown, so every later unit on every sink is dropped: the run exits with nothing printed and an MCP server stops answering. A literal $ in @odata.nextLink is ordinary OData, so real tenants send what killed the run. Tests: internal/exoblackbox/query_class_test.go (each input through the built binaries, seen failing first) and internal/cliutil/kit_readable_test.go (the kit itself as the oracle).

handfixes.summary: A token saved by auth set-token (any SaveTokens call) replaces a stored online_token, which AuthHeader ranks above access_token.
handfixes.why: The generated SaveTokens left a stored online_token in place, so set-token reported success while the next run sent the older token. Test: TestSavedTokenOutranksOlderStoredSlots.

handfixes.summary: The credential store and config writer checks the new temporary file is private before writing any credential bytes, and refuses otherwise.
handfixes.why: A directory with an inherited ACL that lets another user read new files got the token written and published; the permission check ran only afterwards. Test: TestCredentialFileRefusedUnderAnInheritedReadACL (darwin). The generated Windows test TestSaveCredentialsVerifiesWrittenFile asserted the published file; it now asserts the refusal and no file.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored and sync keeps walking, then ends that resource failed with the row ids
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named in a sync_error event and in the resource's error, the run exits non-zero, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows).
